author: agent
text:
Comment rot ANSWERED at 0.57.2, not confirmed away - the comment that flagged was wrong, and the code moved to make it true.

It read: "Always via viz's loader, never by reading the template file directly ... one reader is what keeps the two paths from drifting apart." The claim was one READER, and it was accurate about load_template. But rendering is not loading: viz.render does two substitutions, the data blob and the title, and this function only ever did the first. So there was one loader and two renderers, and they had already drifted - every console page ever served carried a browser tab reading literally "memway - __MEMWAY_TITLE__" while the exported docs/map.html got the repo name. The comment described a discipline the function was not keeping.

Now it calls viz.render, so the console cannot lose a substitution the export performs. Pinned by test_the_served_page_has_a_real_title, falsified by restoring the half-render.

Worth naming the class, because this repo has now hit it twice: 0.54.1 fixed every generated map claiming to be a map of "itsdangerous" in its tab. Both are lesson 11 - a string naming a thing that does not derive from the thing - and both were found by a human looking at a rendered page, not by any test. The general shape is subtler than "don't restate constants": a caller that reimplements PART of a shared renderer inherits the parts it copied and silently drops the parts it did not.

Also new here: the function takes filter_prefix and force and passes them to _map_payload, which is what makes the console honour viz's readability guard instead of overriding it.
